@copilot Please update this PR to pass the `OpenTelemetry` instance into the Couchbase request-tracer factories instead of constructing and passing separate `Tracer` and `Logger` instances from the advice.

For Couchbase 3.0, use `CouchbaseRequestTracer.create(OpenTelemetry openTelemetry)`, build both the tracer and exception logger inside that factory, and simplify the advice to `builder.requestTracer(CouchbaseRequestTracer.create(GlobalOpenTelemetry.get()));`.

For Couchbase 3.1, use `create(OpenTelemetry openTelemetry, boolean legacyBridge)` and move both telemetry construction and the existing instrumentation-name selection into the factory. Preserve `io.opentelemetry.couchbase-3.1` for the legacy bridge and `com.couchbase.client.jvm` otherwise. Couchbase 3.2 already accepts `OpenTelemetry`, so use that factory as the reference.

Keep the existing instrumentation names, schema URLs, and exception-signal behavior unchanged. Update affected callers and tests, and run the relevant tests.

threads.body: [Testing] The `logs` and `logs/dup` tasks only run helper tests with a manually supplied logger. The installed-agent Couchbase tests do not exercise these modes or assert exception logs, so the new logger factory and SDK `RequestSpan.recordException` callback are not tested together. Add an agent-backed failing operation on a supported SDK version that invokes the callback, covering default, `logs`, and `logs/dup` in separate JVMs wired into `check`. Assert span-event selection and the WARN exception log's scope and Couchbase span correlation.

Addressed in 894508ccaae8179194ece824fac527c9456b27ef.

CouchbaseExceptionSignalTest constructs ClusterEnvironment with the installed agent, rather than manually supplying a tracer or logger. It performs a failing SDK 3.4.3 get, checks the SDK-provided CompletionException and its timeout cause, asserts the operation span exception selection, and verifies exactly one WARN db.client.operation.exception log with standard exception attributes, com.couchbase.client.jvm scope, the 1.44.0 schema, and the operation span context. The default suite and filtered logs/logs-dup JVM variants pass and are dependencies of check. Both non-default event profiles are registered and verified in metadata collection.

@copilot Replace only the new standalone manual Test-execution blocks identified below with the suite-owned execution convention introduced by merged PR #20625. The user explicitly chose to limit this follow-up to newly introduced standalone blocks, not partially migrate modules with existing manual-task mixes or restructure custom suites.

Use `testing { suites { named<JvmTestSuite>("test") { executions { ... } } } }`, with one `executions` block per suite. Register each existing variant using its suffix, such as `register("ExceptionSignalLogs")`, preserving the generated task name `testExceptionSignalLogs`. The helper owns the test output, runtime classpath, and check dependencies, so remove the replaced raw `register<Test>` declarations, their redundant source/classpath assignments, and their redundant explicit check wiring. Preserve all filters and variant-only settings on the same variants; do not put filtered selectors into common `configureEach` or narrow the ordinary default test execution. Do not change the helper API or capitalize/decapitalize suffixes differently.

These PR branches currently predate #20625 and do not contain the execution helper. Make the merged convention available by merging the current PR base branch into this PR's existing head branch, preserving the pre-update PR head on the first-parent chain. Do not rebase, force-push, reverse the merge direction, copy the shared helper into this PR, or change another PR's branch. Preserve the existing PR base and draft/ready state.

In `instrumentation/couchbase/couchbase-common-3.0/javaagent-unit-tests/build.gradle.kts`, replace the entire newly added `tasks { ... }` block with default-suite executions. Preserve `testExceptionSignalLogs` and `testExceptionSignalLogsDup` as `register("ExceptionSignalLogs")` and `register("ExceptionSignalLogsDup")`, using the same JVM exception-signal settings of `logs` and `logs/dup`. Keep both variants running the full existing unit-test sources and preserve the default/logs/logs-dup matrix.

These shared unit-test variants currently have no `metadataConfig` label and are not metadata-collection profiles. Keep their JVM settings as ordinary `jvmArgs` or equivalent system properties; do not introduce `telemetryConfig`, metadata labels, or collection registrations for them.

Leave `instrumentation/couchbase/couchbase-3.2/javaagent/build.gradle.kts` and its existing manual-task mix unchanged. In particular, retain its latest-dependency exception-signal coverage, version343Test/version344Test compatibility suites, and all existing integration and collection wiring. Do not restore a logs-dup integration task.

Keep this a behavior-preserving Gradle refactor. Preserve dependencies, Java-version constraints, normal test coverage, telemetry-profile labels or deliberate lack of labels, and metadata collection registrations. Do not change production code or test assertions, add or remove execution variants, or migrate unrelated files. Run repository formatting and the focused checks that cover the migrated variants. Update this existing PR rather than opening a new one. Acceptance: only the listed new standalone execution blocks use the new convention, their current execution matrix and selection are unchanged, and every migrated task is still included in check through the helper.

replies.body: Migrated the shared unit-test variants to suite-owned executions in `97e4934`; the default, `logs`, and `logs/dup` tasks pass, and the `check` dry run includes both variants.
